text:
maya: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need to decide where the 'rateproof' handoff lives between edge proxies and the central quota service. proposal: keep fast admission checks at the edge but push abuse scoring + long-window reconciliation to central. thoughts?

gavin: +1 for edges doing fast gates. latency is king for hosted paths. but we need a clear contract for what the edge can assume about quota state.

arjun: agree. the contract matters. propose a three-field admission response from central: `allowed(bool)`, `soft_allow(bool)`, `lease_ttl_ms(int)` — edges treat `soft_allow` as best-effort and proactively sample telemetry if `soft_allow=true`.

samira: just to call out tradeoffs: `soft_allow` reduces false rejections during transient spikes but increases potential abuse surface if edges over-trust. we should bound how many `soft_allow` tokens an edge can grant per tenant per minute.

maya: exactly. thinking naming the mechanism `rateproof` — a bounded, locally-consumable buffer that central leases to edges. edges can consume without blocking, central reconciles periodically.

gavin: how do we ensure observability? ops needs per-tenant mismatch telemetry: central allocations vs edge consumption, plus sampled traces when reconciliation drops tokens.

arjun: we can emit three lightweight events from edge: `edge.admit(local)`, `edge.reconcile(used,leased_id)`, `edge.reject(reason)`. Keep payload tiny: tenant_id, leased_id, delta, seq. wireproto proto sketch: ```message EdgeEvent { string tenant = 1; string lease_id = 2; int64 delta = 3; int64 ts_ms = 4; enum Kind { ADMIT=0; RECONCILE=1; REJECT=2;} Kind kind = 5; }```

samira: nice. also add a sampling flag for heavy clients so we can attach a trace_id occasionally: `trace_hint` field — opt-in by tenant.

maya: question about abuse detection: should scoring run at edge (fast heuristics) or only central? my read: edge runs cheap heuristics (rate windows, short burst entropy) and tags requests; central runs heavier ML signals and can revoke leases.

gavin: that makes sense. edge heuristics could be simple token-drop rules and pattern detectors. central does ML + historical churn analysis and can reduce future lease sizes. when central revokes or reduces leases, how should it signal back? delta push vs explicit revoke?

arjun: prefer explicit revoke push over eventual reduction. edges should accept push with a `revocation_id` and apply immediate soft-decrease to local buffers, then fully enforce on next reconcile heartbeat. push path payload small: `tenant, revoke_id, new_lease_size, reason_code`.

samira: what about failure modes? if central is partitioned, edges must be conservative. fallback: edges enter degraded mode where they halve local buffers and sample 1% of rejects to central when connectivity returns.

maya: operational playbook: 1) central sends revocation push; 2) edges apply soft-decrease; 3) reconcile window (30s) to fully enforce; 4) ops dashboard highlights tenants with >10% reconciliation loss.

gavin: perf numbers we should aim for: edge admit path <2ms p50, reconcile heartbeat <= 100ms RTT to central, push latency ideally <200ms.

arjun: also need a compact encoding for lease ids and a signing MAC so edges can prove a lease is genuine if they get audited. 8-12 byte lease id + 16-byte HMAC should be fine.

samira: can we avoid storing per-lease state centrally? we could use token buckets keyed by tenant shard and include a monotonic counter in lease id to make reconciliation idempotent.

maya: good call. minimize central state explosion. central keeps only per-tenant counters + max outstanding leased. edges track local seq windows.

gavin: one more UX ask: product wants a visible metric `leased_buffer_utilization` per tenant in console and an alert when utilization > 80% for 5m. ops-bot should create an alert template.

ops-bot: Alert template created: `edge.leased_buffer_utilization > 0.8 for 5m` -> Pager (oncall-eng-infra) ; doc: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rateproof-alerts> :white_check_mark:

maya: next steps: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with the proto sketches, failure modes, and the ops playbook. target review by EOD Friday. if anyone wants to take the proto PR, shout now. :slightly_smiling_face:

arjun: I'll pick up the proto PR. will start with the EdgeEvent message + lease id HMAC fields.

samira: I'll draft the ops playbook & dashboard panel queries.

gavin: planning note — update the edge-side SDK to expose `soft_allow` semantics to app teams, plus a deprecation window for callers who depend on deterministic rejects.

maya: awesome, thanks. linking notes: <https://redwood.internal/doc/rateproof-rfc-draft> and the reconcile bench results: `bench/reconcile/2024-06-05.md`.

maya: tagging for follow-up: @gavin @arjun @samira
